description: Phase 8 Auto-remediation overview. The on-call landing page after a successful Alertmanager firing: see what auto-remediation has done in the last 24h, what is currently in cooldown, and which alerts are triggering the most. Source tables: `remediation_history` + `remediation_cooldowns` in PostgreSQL (per `db/migrations/V003__phase8_remediation.sql`). For the live cooldown list, the dashboard reads `GET /remediation/cooldowns` from the in-process axum server (provisioned in `observability/grafana/provisioning/datasources/datasources.yml`); the JSON datasource plugin is required for that panel.
title: Auto-remediation Overview (80-01)

panels.title: 24h remediation executions (total)
panels.description: Count of every `remediation_history` row written in the last 24h. Includes both succeeded and failed attempts. The retry_count column is summed separately; this panel is the total *attempts*.

targets.rawSql: SELECT count(*)::int AS total FROM remediation_history WHERE executed_at > now() - interval '24 hours'

panels.title: 24h success rate
panels.description: Fraction of remediation_history rows in the last 24h whose `outcome='succeeded'`. A value below 80% means auto-remediation is firing but not landing — most likely a wrong runbook, a permission issue, or an upstream problem the runbook cannot fix.

targets.rawSql: SELECT (count(*) FILTER (WHERE outcome='succeeded'))::float / greatest(count(*), 1) AS success_rate, count(*)::int AS total FROM remediation_history WHERE executed_at > now() - interval '24 hours'

panels.title: Active cooldowns
panels.description: Number of rows in `remediation_cooldowns` whose `expires_at > now()`. These are actions the engine will NOT re-execute until the cooldown window elapses. If this number is large and growing, see panel 6 for the longest-running ones.

targets.rawSql: SELECT count(*)::int AS active FROM remediation_cooldowns WHERE expires_at > now()

panels.title: Distinct actions triggered (24h)
panels.description: Count of distinct `action_id` values seen in the last 24h. A jump in this number means a new runbook is firing — confirm it is intentional.

targets.rawSql: SELECT count(DISTINCT action_id)::int AS distinct_actions FROM remediation_history WHERE executed_at > now() - interval '24 hours'

panels.title: 24h remediation count by action (timeline)
panels.description: Time-bucketed count of remediation_history rows, broken out by `action_id`. Stack mode (`stack` option) makes it easy to see both which actions are firing and the absolute volume. A flat-line is healthy; spikes correlate with incident clusters.

targets.rawSql: SELECT $__timeGroupAlias(executed_at, '15m'), action_id AS metric, count(*)::int AS value FROM remediation_history WHERE $__timeFilter(executed_at) GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Top 5 triggered alerts (24h)
panels.description: The 5 most-fired alert_name values in the last 24h, with their success / failure split. This is the 'what is hurting us right now' panel — actionable: each row is a candidate for a new or improved runbook.

targets.rawSql: SELECT alert_name, count(*)::int AS total, count(*) FILTER (WHERE outcome='succeeded')::int AS succeeded, count(*) FILTER (WHERE outcome='failed')::int AS failed FROM remediation_history WHERE executed_at > now() - interval '24 hours' GROUP BY alert_name ORDER BY total DESC LIMIT 5

panels.title: Active cooldowns (live)
panels.description: Read from the in-process axum server's `GET /remediation/cooldowns` endpoint. Requires the Grafana JSON / Infinity datasource plugin. Shows action_id + expires_at (UTC). Expired rows are filtered out by the engine.

panels.title: Recent failure log (24h)
panels.description: Most recent 50 rows where `outcome='failed'`. The `error_msg` column contains the engine's step-0 failure description (e.g. `step 0: command not found`). Filter by `action_id` or `alert_name` to narrow.

targets.rawSql: SELECT executed_at, action_id, alert_name, retry_count, error_msg FROM remediation_history WHERE outcome='failed' AND executed_at > now() - interval '24 hours' ORDER BY executed_at DESC LIMIT 50
